gold.comment: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

gold.comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: A global grant is silently ignored once any per-client resource exists, denying legitimate admins in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`. Check the per-client resource from `findByName` and then the all-clients type resource from `getResourceTypeResource` so either grant succeeds.

gold.comment: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning boolean. WHY: Caller AbstractTokenExchangeProvider expects a boolean deny/allow and will propagate 500 on every token-exchange when V2 is enabled, breaking the contract that V1 satisfies by returning false. HOW: Return false (or implement V2 evaluation) instead of throwing.

gold.comment: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: After the server stops blocking the address (e.g. an admin removes the `BlockedEmail` rule), the user still cannot submit because `emailValidation` returns failed from the stale `rejectedEmails` entry, and this persists for the lifetime of the controller. Clear or remove entries from `rejectedEmails` when the email input changes, or reset it when the modal is reopened.

gold.comment: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), but individual group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never get their type set to "Groups" — getOrCreateResource calls resourceStore.create(...) (which takes no type) and never calls resource.setType(...), whereas only the all-groups resource gets setType("Groups") in AdminPermissionsSchema.init (line 274); V1 sets it explicitly at GroupPermissions.java:117 (`groupResource.setType("Group")`). As a result findByType returns none of the per-group resources, so a caller's per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never enumerated and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns an empty/incorrect set. This makes UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource's group-based user restriction (which feed the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute) return wrong results for fine-grained admins. Set the resource type to "Groups" when creating individual group resources (or enumerate via findByName/store lookups instead of type) so that group-scoped permissions are actually discovered.

gold.comment: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: hasPermission() passes the result of getResourceTypeResource(...) to policyStore.findByResource() without a null check. HOW: return false if the type resource is null.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: EventManager is built with the credentials of the acting user (ctx.user), not the booking organizer (booking.user.credentials, which is already loaded). finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The new disabled-feature test only verifies the error text, not the failure exit status. If the metadata command still prints this diagnostic but exits with 0 (or another incorrect code) instead of FEATURE_DISABLED (4), this test would still pass. Assert that cliResult.exitCode() equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED so the test actually protects the new disabled-feature failure contract.

gold.comment: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

gold.comment: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The start-bound check only rejects slots that end at or before the override start; it never checks whether the slot starts before the override. WHY: A slot that begins before the override window and ends inside it is treated as available, so fixed hosts can be booked partly outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotStartTime is before the override start.

gold.comment: The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: The override date is formatted with `dayjs(...)`, which uses the server's local timezone, while the slot date is formatted in UTC. WHY: On a server not running in UTC, the day comparison is off for overrides near midnight, so overrides get applied to the wrong day or skipped. HOW: Use dayjs.utc(date.start) before adding the offset and formatting.

gold.comment: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls are not awaited, and they now perform the DB update or delete (`cancelled: true` or row deletion) themselves. The old code awaited its `deleteMany` promises. In a serverless handler the work can be cut off after the response, so reminders may never be marked cancelled and will still be sent. Fix: collect the returned promises and `await Promise.all(...)` them before returning. Apply the same fix to the equivalent unawaited calls in bookings.tsx and workflows.tsx.

gold.comment: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The default cancellation path only marks the reminder as cancelled, even when its scheduled send is less than ten minutes away. Booking cancellation and reschedule-request callers use this path, so they no longer attempt immediate provider cancellation, and the cron cannot reliably cancel the send because SendGrid requires cancellations more than ten minutes before delivery; a cron run after delivery also deletes the row before processing cancellations. Cancel at the provider immediately when handling near-term reminders rather than relying exclusively on deferred processing.

gold.comment: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

gold.comment: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

+class EmbedController < ApplicationController
+  skip_before_filter :check_xhr
+  skip_before_filter :preload_json
+  before_filter :ensure_embeddable
+

+

gold.comment: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: A plain `Error` is thrown when the credential is missing or not owned by the user. tRPC turns this into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logs it as a server fault, instead of returning a proper client error. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found or access denied" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

gold.comment: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The handler directly constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`initFromCredentialId()`, which checks the `calendar-cache` feature flag and returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when disabled. When the feature is off globally, this still executes a `CalendarCache` `groupBy` query on every connectedCalendars call for no benefit and can expose stale cache status. Use the existing `CalendarCache.init*` factory or gate the query with the feature flag.

gold.comment: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

gold.comment: The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Constructor accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional for every scope, but the zod schema still requires `teamId` when `scope` is `"team"`. A caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId` and compile successfully, yet runtime validation fails and the service silently returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`, hiding the caller bug. Restore the stricter `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` type for the constructor parameter, or throw a validation error instead of silently failing closed.

gold.comment: Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: When a caller embeds the result as `WHERE ${base} AND <extra>`, SQL operator precedence turns it into `A OR (B AND extra)`, which can leak rows outside the authorization scope or ignore the extra predicate. Always wrap the fragment `getBaseConditions` returns in parentheses, using `Prisma.sql` for `authConditions` and `filterConditions`, and wrap the eventTypeId OR-fragment in its own parentheses.

+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.

+    def __init__(self) -> None:

+        self.last_committed: dict[Partition, int] = {}
+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}

+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())

+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):

+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)

+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:

+                if not all_offsets:

+                outstanding = self.outstanding[partition]
+                last_committed = self.last_committed.get(partition, -1)

+                min_offset = min(all_offsets)
+                max_offset = max(all_offsets)

+                start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)

+T = TypeVar("T")

+@dataclass
+class WorkItem(Generic[T]):
+    """Work item that includes the original message for offset tracking."""
+
+    partition: Partition
+    offset: int
+    result: T
+    message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]

+class OffsetTracker:
+    """
+    Tracks outstanding offsets and determines which offsets are safe to commit.

+    - Tracks offsets per partition
+    - Only commits offsets when all prior offsets are processed
+    - Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks

+    def __init__(self) -> None:

+        self.partition_locks: dict[Partition, threading.Lock] = {}
+
+    def _get_partition_lock(self, partition: Partition) -> threading.Lock:
+        """Get or create a lock for a partition."""
+        lock = self.partition_locks.get(partition)
+        if lock:
+            return lock
+        return self.partition_locks.setdefault(partition, threading.Lock())
+
+    def add_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Record that we've started processing an offset."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):
+            self.all_offsets[partition].add(offset)
+            self.outstanding[partition].add(offset)

+    def complete_offset(self, partition: Partition, offset: int) -> None:
+        """Mark an offset as completed."""
+        with self._get_partition_lock(partition):

+    def get_committable_offsets(self) -> dict[Partition, int]:

gold.comment: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: `self.downsize` is defined twice — lines 145-147 (`downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`) and lines 149-151 (`downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). Ruby lets the later definition win, so the 4-positional-arg form is silently replaced by the 3-arg form. WHY: `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (given 5, expected 3..4)`, crashing the ResizeEmoji job on every run. HOW: delete the redundant definition — keep only the dimensions-string variant (or rename one of them) and update the emoji job to pass `"100x100"` accordingly.

gold.comment: The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: tempfile.path is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with runs it in a shell through backticks without escaping. For API URL uploads, that path contains the request-controlled `type` param (`discourse-upload-#{type}`). WHY: A `type` containing shell metacharacters such as `$(...)` or `;` runs arbitrary commands on the server when the oversized image is downsized. HOW: Restrict `type` to a whitelist (or Shellwords-escape every argument in convert_with) before the path reaches the shell.

gold.comment: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: remove_member passes a bare integer (`user_id`) to `group.users.delete(...)`, but `users` is a `has_many :through` collection whose `delete(*records)` expects associated record objects, not primary keys. WHY: unlike `destroy`, `delete` does not coerce numeric ids (see admin/users_controller.rb:128, which correctly passes `@user`), so this raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` and returns a 500 without removing the member (or, if unhandled by the association, deletes the wrong row). HOW: load the record first — `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` — or reuse the existing model helper `group.remove(User.find(user_id))` (group.rb:276), which deletes the group_users join row.

gold.comment: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Computed keys using Zod schema objects' toString() do not define dynamic properties, and this z.object strips actual expiry fields such as expires_in and expiry_date. With syncing enabled, Zoom subsequently computes expiry_date from missing newTokens.expires_in, producing NaN, while Office365 loses its refreshed expiry. Define the supported expiry properties explicitly and preserve required provider fields with passthrough or a suitable catchall.

gold.comment: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The new credential update references prisma without importing or defining it in this module; searching this file finds only this use. This introduces a TypeScript unresolved-name error and a ReferenceError when Salesforce client initialization reaches the update. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma.

gold.comment: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: Success is checked with `response.statusText !== "OK"`. statusText is empty on HTTP/2 and some runtimes, so valid 200 responses are treated as errors and throw an HttpError. Fix: check `response.ok` instead.

gold.comment: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent:
WHAT: After fetching and persisting a new access token, the `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh value) rather than the just-obtained `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.
WHY: The connection that this block refreshes for is authenticated with the stale/expired token it was supposed to replace, so the refresh has no effect on the returned connection and requests can fail with an expired session.
HOW: Use the refreshed token when building the connection, e.g. `accessToken: accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

gold.comment: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The webhook indexes appStoreMetadata using the database app slug, but that map is keyed by integration directory names. For example, Google credentials use appId 'google-calendar' while apps.metadata.generated.ts exposes the metadata under 'googlecalendar', so a valid Google sync request returns 404. Resolve the metadata by its slug value instead of assuming the map key equals the database slug.

gold.comment: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

gold.comment: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The span buffer keys `span-buf:s:{...}` were changed from plain sets to sorted sets (Python `sadd`→`zadd`, Lua `scard`/`sunionstore`→`zcard`/`zunionstore`), but the key names were not versioned. During/after a rolling deploy, keys written by the previous code still exist as sets for up to the redis TTL (3600s); the new `zadd` (and `zcard`/`zunionstore` in add-buffer.lua) then fail with WRONGTYPE, raising in process_batch and stalling the consumer until the keys expire. Fix: version/rename the buffer keys (or perform a one-time migration) so old set-typed keys are not read as sorted sets.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness self.initial_data.get(age/timestamp) so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypass mutual-exclusion. WHY: a report containing both age and timestamp with a zero value incorrectly validates, breaking Working-Draft vs Editors-Draft exclusivity. HOW: check key presence (e.g. in self.initial_data) instead of truthiness.

finding.label: security
finding.suggestionContent: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

gold.comment: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The custom body renderer is accepted only when its return value is truthy, despite the API specifying that only undefined triggers fallback. Valid React results such as 0, an empty string, or null are replaced by the default field renderer, producing incorrect content or defeating deliberate cell suppression. Check cell !== undefined, and apply the same contract to the header renderer.

gold.comment: Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.

finding.label: performance
finding.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every paginated GET now runs query_replay_instance and then a nodestore get_multi over all of the replay's error_ids, with no cap and before pagination. WHY: a replay with many errors loads every full event payload from nodestore on every page request, which adds large latency and memory use to a request that already calls Seer. HOW: cap error_ids (e.g. error_ids[:N]) before calling fetch_error_details.

gold.comment: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The restarted-path kill guard `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` is always False for the processes this class creates, because they come from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` (as the annotation on line 68 states), which is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`.
WHY: When a flusher process crashes or hangs, `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement for the same shards while the previous process is never killed (`process.kill()` is skipped) and is never joined; for the hang case the stuck process is still alive and can resume flushing the same shards concurrently with its replacement, producing duplicate segments to buffered-segments. This is a regression: the pre-PR code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, which worked for these spawn processes.
HOW: Guard against the actual type, e.g. `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess): process.kill()` (or `hasattr(process, "kill")`), and/or compare against the same base class used to build it, so spawned processes are killed before replacement.

gold.comment: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

finding.label: bug
finding.suggestionContent: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

deterministic.existingCode:
def website_name
    website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil
    discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname
    return if website_host.nil?
    if website_host == discourse_host
      # example.com == example.com
      website_host + URI(website.to_s).path
    elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
      # www.example.com == forum.example.com
      website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
    else
      # example.com == forum.example.com
      discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
    end
  end
